title.en: Protecting special places: Silent Valley and protected areas

text.en: A dam was planned in a Kerala rainforest, but villagers, students and scientists joined the Save Silent Valley Movement.

The Silent Valley National Park in Kerala is a rainforest home to rare plants and animals. Unlike other rainforests that buzz with cicadas, it was silent, which gave the valley its name.
A dam planned here would have flooded the forest. People from all over joined the Save Silent Valley Movement and stopped it. Today it is a protected forest.
Protected areas are forests, rivers or hills kept safe by the government for animals, plants and nature. People may not cut trees or harm animals there.
The Western Ghats have over 50 protected areas such as wildlife sanctuaries, national parks and tiger reserves, which protect the lion-tailed macaque, tiger, elephant and hornbill.
Shanti's family then heads to Kanyakumari, the southernmost point of the mainland, where three seas meet.
Every place has something special to teach us. People live differently but everywhere depend on nature and care for it in their own way.
Mawsynram in Meghalaya is the wettest inhabited place on Earth.
Let us reflect: what surprised you, which place would you like to visit, and how is your region similar to one in the story?
(additional, not in the textbook) You can start by caring for a tree, a bird or a pond near you.
